title: IMUNON Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Update
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about IMUNON INC.'s business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: IMUNON Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Update August 11, 2026 PDF Version IMNN-001 is the first frontline treatment candidate to demonstrate the potential for a clinically meaningful overall survival benefit in women newly diagnosed with ovarian cancer Enrollment in the Phase 3 OVATION 3 Study of IMNN-001 is expected to be completed by the first half of 2029, supported by strong Phase 2 clinical data showing significant overall survival benefit Company to hold conference call today at 11:00 a.m. EDT LAWRENCEVILLE, N.J., Aug. 11, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- IMUNON , Inc. (NASDAQ: IMNN) , a clinical-stage company in late-stage development with its DNA-mediated immunotherapy, today reported financial results for the three months and six months ended June 30, 2026, and highlighted recent business updates including progress in advancing Phase 3 clinical development of its lead candidate IMNN-001 in newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer. “The second quarter brought continued momentum for IMNN-001,” said Stacy Lindborg, Ph.D., President and Chief Executive Officer of IMUNON. “Enrollment in our pivotal Phase 3 OVATION 3 study continues to exceed our planning assumptions, reflecting the compelling survival data generated in OVATION 2, our highly favorable safety profile, and growing confidence among investigators in IMNN-001’s potential to improve outcomes for women with newly diagnosed advanced ovarian cancer.” “We were also encouraged by new preliminary data from our ongoing Phase 2 minimal residual disease (MRD) study, which showed a deeper antitumor response in patients treated with IMNN-001, including higher rates of circulating tumor DNA clearance and no evidence of disease following frontline therapy. We believe these findings provide further independent evidence of IMNN-001’s biological activity and reinforce the mechanism underlying the survival benefit observed in the OVATION 2 study, while we remain fully focused on our highest priority of efficiently advancing OVATION 3. title: Support Long-Term Joint Health as You Age
summary: We often joke about our bones becoming creaky as we grow older due to decades of walking, bending, lifting, and moving adding up.
body_text: We often joke about our bones becoming creaky as we grow older due to decades of walking, bending, lifting, and moving adding up. So, it makes sense that your joints don’t feel like they did in your younger years. It’s natural wear and tear on your body. A joint is just two bones meeting. Knee, shoulder, hip, doesn’t matter which one. The problem that your body must solve is to keep those bones from grinding against each other every time you move, over days, months, and years. Cartilage is the perfect solution. It covers the ends of the bones. It’s smooth and a little squishy, sort of like a rubber cap on a chair leg that keeps it from scratching the floor. There’s also fluid that fills the joint space so bones glide instead of grind. Ligaments hold the bones to each other. Think sturdy straps, keeping the joint from wobbling side to side. Tendons do something different. They connect muscle to bone, and that connection is the whole reason flexing a muscle causes movement. Every time you move, cartilage cushions the impact, fluid keeps things slick, ligaments keep the joint stable, and tendons turn muscle power into motion. When one part wears down, the rest work harder to cover it. Why Cartilage Doesn’t Bounce Back Here’s the part most people don’t know. Cartilage has no blood supply.¹ None. Most tissue in your body heals by sending blood straight to the injury, repair cells and nutrients included. Cartilage can’t do that. It’s stuck getting nutrition from joint fluid soaking in as you move, which is slow, and not exactly efficient. So once cartilage wears down, there’s no repair crew showing up. It doesn’t grow back the way a cut on your skin closes up. This is one of those cases where prevention matters more than treatment, because once damage happens, the options are limited. Why Tendons Take Longer to Heal with Age Tendons age differently than cartilage, but you end up in a similar place: slower healing. The tissue inside a tendon doesn’t replace itself very often. The same cells and fibers can stay there for years, even decades.² As we get older, the cells responsible for maintaining tendon tissue become less active. At the same time, the fibers in the tendon slowly change, forming more connections, called cross-links. In simple terms, this makes the tendon stiffer, less flexible, and more likely to tear. None of that means a tendon is doomed. It means an injury that healed in a couple months at age 30 might take longer at age 60 and sometimes needs more help getting there. Movement Is Still the Best Medicine It may be surprising to you, but less movement is usually worse for aging joints, not better. Cartilage gets its nutrients from the fluid that moves through the joint during activity.3 Stay still too long, and that joint stiffens up due to the lack of nutrients. Keep moving, even gently, and you’re feeding the tissues that need it most. Low-impact activities like walking, swimming, and cycling let you stay active without hammering your joints like higher-impact sports. Strength training and proper stretching matter just as much. Strong muscles around a joint take pressure off the joint itself, which is one of the simplest ways to protect cartilage that’s already under strain. Signs It’s Worth a Doctor’s Visit Most day-to-day stiffness isn’t a big deal. A few things are worth getting checked out, though, rather than waiting and hoping they pass: Pain or swelling that sticks around for more than a few days Morning stiffness that takes 30 to 60 minutes or longer to loosen up A joint that feels unstable, locks up, or has lost a noticeable amount of range of motion Pain that’s started messing with basic stuff, like climbing stairs or getting out of a chair If any of that sounds familiar, it’s worth asking your doctor what’s going on. Regenerative Medicine for Joint Health Tendon Tears A tendon tear at age 60 doesn’t heal the way it would have at age 30. Slower-recovering tissue means healing often takes longer, and in some cases, the body needs additional support to heal well. That’s why we’ve developed the Integrity Implant : a partially resorbable scaffold made from hyaluronic acid, or HA, a substance your body already produces. HA plays an essential role throughout your body, in everything from joint lubrication to skin hydration, so it’s something your body knows well. Integrity is used in tendon repairs, including commonly injured tendons like the rotator cuff and Achilles tendon , and it’s designed to support your body’s natural healing process. It has a woven design that leaves space for your body’s own healing cells to move in and rebuild tendon tissue at the repair site. It’s reinforced with a medical-grade type of polyester, a material that many sutures are made of, to make it stronger so your doctor can place it in the precise location on your tendon injury. Cartilage Injuries For some people, the problem isn’t a torn tendon, it’s a small area of damaged cartilage, known as a “lesion” that won’t heal easily on its own. These cartilage problems are often caused by an injury, such as a sprain, or by repeated strain on the joint over time, rather than general wear and tear. Hyalofast is an HA-based scaffold designed to support the body’s natural healing by encouraging new cartilage growth at the site of the lesion.* The goal is to help repair the damaged area, rather than simply treating the pain associated with it. Aging Joints, Not Aging Out Joint changes are part of getting older, but joint pain doesn’t have to keep you on the sidelines. Staying active, building strength, and knowing what options exist if an injury or wear and tear catch up with you are all part of the same goal: staying in motion for the long run. If you’re noticing joint pain or changes in how your joints feel, talk to your doctor about what may be causing it and what can help. * Hyalofast is not available in the United States. Integrity is available in the US and select markets outside of the United States. Anika products may not be available in all geographies. Product availability is subject to the regulatory clearances in individual markets. References Arthritis Foundation. Osteoarthritis. https://www.arthritis.org/diseases/osteoarthritis Effect of Aging on Tendon Biology, Biomechanics and Implications for Treatment Approaches. National Library of Medicine. https://www.mdpi.com/1422-0067/24/20/15183 Arthritis Foundation. 8 Ways Exercise Helps Your Joints. https://www.arthritis.org/health-wellness/healthy-living/physical-activity/getting-started/8-ways-exercise-helps-joints (opens in a new tab)

title: Best AI Video Summarizers [2026]
summary: The best AI video summarizer depends on captions. Verified prices, what each tool accepts, and which fits lectures, meetings, or conference talks.
body_text: The best AI video summarizer for you depends on something no vendor page leads with: whether your video has captions. Most tools in this category never touch the video. They pull the transcript and hand it to a language model, which is why Google states plainly that only the text transcript of a YouTube video gets imported into its own notebook product. Once you know that, the category sorts itself. This roundup covers YouTube's built-in tools, Gemini Notebook, NoteGPT, Eightify, Notta, and Fireflies, with prices verified in August 2026, plus a note about one well-known tool that is offline. What Does an AI Video Summarizer Actually Do? An AI video summarizer converts a video's spoken audio into text, feeds that text to a language model, and returns a condensed written version of what was said. That is the entire pipeline, and it runs in three steps: Get a transcript. Either reuse captions the platform already generated, or run automatic speech recognition (ASR) on the audio. Send the transcript to a language model with an instruction like "summarize the key points with timestamps." Format the output as bullets, a mind map, an outline, or chat answers. Steps two and three are near identical across every tool here. Step one is where they differ, and it is the expensive one: ASR costs the vendor real money per minute, which is why it appears as a metered limit while caption-based summarizing gets advertised as unlimited. Captions are also less reliable than most people assume. YouTube's automatic captions cover more than 90 languages, and Google is candid about the trade-off: captions "might misrepresent the spoken content due to mispronunciations, accents, dialects, or background noise." Google lists six reasons captions may not appear at all, among them poor sound quality, an unsupported language, and several people speaking at once. Any one of those turns a summarizer into an error message on a video that plays perfectly. A summarizer is only ever as good as the transcript it never shows you. When the summary comes back thin, the transcript is usually thinner. If you are using video to build a skill rather than to skim one, AI tools and courses for learning to code is a better starting point. Summaries are for triage, not practice. The Best AI Video Summarizers in 2026, Compared Tool Input it accepts Video without captions Output Price (verified August 2026) Best for YouTube transcript and Ask YouTube Any video you are watching No On-screen answers, no export Free Deciding whether to watch Gemini Notebook Captioned YouTube URLs, audio and video uploads Only for uploads Notes, briefings, chat across sources Free tier, 50 sources Whole modules and course collections NoteGPT YouTube URLs, playlists, local audio and video Yes, with a minute cap Summaries, mind maps, timestamped notes Pro $9/mo billed annually Volume, playlists, uncaptioned video Eightify YouTube, in browser or on mobile Not stated Timestamped key points $9.99/mo or $59.99/yr on the App Store Skimming one video at a time Notta Uploads, live meetings, Zoom, Teams, Meet Yes Transcript plus AI summary Free tier; Pro $8.17/mo annually Recordings you already have Fireflies Meetings it joins, audio and video uploads Yes Transcript, summary, action items Free forever; Pro $10 per seat/mo annually Recurring team calls Any chatbot, with a pasted transcript Whatever you can copy No Whatever shape you ask for Inside a plan you likely already pay for Full control of the output Every price came from the vendor's own pricing page or store listing, all linked in Sources. This category re-prices and rebrands unusually fast, so check before subscribing. YouTube's Own Tools Are Free and Already Installed Two YouTube features get confused with each other, and only one is AI. The first is the transcript panel: free, available on any captioned video, and it hands you plain text you can copy. It is not a summarizer, but it is the raw material every summarizer runs on. The second is Ask YouTube on the watch page , which "lets you interact with AI to learn more about the content" of whatever you are watching. Google's documentation puts it at signed-in users aged 13 and over, across more than 190 countries, in 42 languages, on Android, iOS, the web, and TV. Google is unusually direct about the limits. Quality and accuracy "may vary," the tool "may sometimes produce inaccurate or offensive information," and answers are not medical, legal, or financial advice. The verdict: Ask YouTube is excellent at asking and useless at exporting . It will tell you whether a 90 minute talk deserves your evening, but it hands you nothing you can paste into your notes, and does nothing for video hosted elsewhere. Gemini Notebook Is the Best Free Option If Your Video Has Captions The constraint comes first, because it disqualifies a lot of videos. Google's documentation states that "only public YouTube videos with captions, either user-uploaded or auto-generated, are supported," and that "only the text transcript of the video is imported as a source." A second constraint bites harder in practice. Videos uploaded less than 72 hours earlier may not be importable yet, so summarizing a conference talk the morning it goes live often fails. Where Gemini Notebook beats every dedicated summarizer is scale sideways. The free tier holds 50 sources per notebook, each up to 500,000 words or 200MB. A whole conference track, or a semester of recordings, sits in one notebook you can query as a whole rather than video by video. For files you own it also solves the caption problem, since uploaded audio and video are transcribed at import. A lecture recording on your laptop works, even though the same file uploaded uncaptioned to YouTube would not. NoteGPT and Eightify: The Dedicated YouTube Summarizers These are the browser-first tools most people mean by "AI video summarizer," and they differ in one place that matters. NoteGPT is the only tool here that publicly prices the uncaptioned case. On Pro, YouTube videos with subtitles are unlimited, videos without subtitles are capped at 120 minutes each, and local uploads at 1GB. It also batches up to 20 videos at once, plus whole playlists and channels. One inconsistency worth flagging: NoteGPT's YouTube summarizer page advertises videos "up to 150 minutes" without subtitles, while its pricing page sets the Pro limit at 120. Where marketing and pricing disagree, pricing is the page you are buying. From its pricing page : Pro is $9 per month billed annually ($108 a year) or $9.99 month to month, Unlimited is $19.92 per month annually, and Max is $69 per month annually. Eightify is the lighter option: a browser extension and mobile app producing timestamped key points, with summaries and translations in 40 or more languages on videos of any length. Its pricing is harder to pin down, which is itself a fact about the product. The /pricing path returns Not Found, so the only verifiable numbers sit on Apple's App Store listing : $9.99 monthly and $59.99 annually. A tool that will not show its price on its own website is telling you something. Between the two: Choose NoteGPT for volume, playlists, or videos with no usable captions. Choose Eightify for a lightweight skim button inside the browser, when you never need to export a batch. A Note on Summarize.tech Summarize.tech appears in nearly every older listicle on this topic. As of 6 August 2026, it does not respond. Three separate requests through two different edge regions returned HTTP 503 with the code DEPLOYMENT_PAUSED , which is the hosting platform reporting a paused deployment rather than an overload. It may come back, so check rather than reading this as an obituary. But if you arrived here from a 2024 recommendation, that is why the link is dead. The lesson outlives the tool: whatever you build a workflow on, make sure you can export your summaries out of it. Meeting Recordings Are a Different Product Category Consumer YouTube summarizers fail on meetings for structural reasons: several people talk over each other, there are no captions, and the recording lives inside Zoom, Teams, or Meet rather than at a public URL. Fireflies joins the call as a participant. Its free tier gives unlimited transcription but only 400 minutes of storage per team and 20 AI credits, and storage is the limit that actually bites. Pro at $10 per seat per month billed annually raises storage to 8,000 minutes and unlocks downloads. Business at $19 removes the cap; Enterprise at $39 adds private storage and a transcript-only mode. Notta imports rather than attends. Its free plan covers 120 transcription minutes a month, three minutes per conversation, 50 uploads and 10 AI summaries. Pro at $8.17 per month billed annually raises that to 1,800 minutes and five hours per recording; Business at $16.67 makes transcription unlimited. Notta supports 58 languages, integrates with Zoom, Teams, and Meet, and offers a 50% education discount. One thing deserves thought before you switch either on: a bot that joins every call records other people, not only you. Fireflies keeps private storage and its transcript-only mode on Enterprise, so on cheaper plans your recordings sit in a vendor's system in full. Under an NDA, that is a procurement decision, not a preference. Just Paste the Transcript Into a Chatbot Nobody sells you this option, which is why it stays underrated. Open the transcript panel, copy the text, paste it into whichever assistant you already pay for, and ask for exactly the shape you want. The advantages are real: no new subscription, no extra company holding your data, total control of the format. So are the costs: you lose clickable timestamps, the process is manual, and a three hour transcript can overflow a model's context window. Four instructions worth keeping, in rough order of usefulness: "List only the claims the speaker supports with evidence, and name the evidence." Separates argument from assertion faster than any summary. "List what the speaker asserts without support." The inverse, and often the more interesting half. "Produce a timestamped outline, one line per section." Rebuilds the navigation the transcript threw away. "Rewrite this as a checklist for someone who has not watched it." Forces concrete steps instead of themes. Getting more out of this route is a prompting skill that transfers everywhere else, and Scrimba's roundup of prompt engineering courses covers the technique. One caveat applies to every tool here. FaithBench , a benchmark built from summaries produced by 10 modern language models across 8 model families, found that even the best hallucination detectors reach roughly 50% accuracy at spotting an unfaithful summary. Nothing will catch it for you, so when the stakes are real, spot-check against the transcript. Which AI Video Summarizer Should You Use? Choose on two variables: where the video lives, and whether it has captions. Everything else is preference. The student summarizing lecture recordings If the recording is on YouTube with captions, use Gemini Notebook. It is free, and the 50-source limit means a whole module lives in one notebook you can query across rather than video by video. If it is a downloaded file with no captions, use NoteGPT, or Notta, whose education discount makes it cheaper across a full term of recordings. One honest note: a summary is a revision aid, not a substitute for the work. If you cannot reconstruct the argument without rereading it, you have not learned it. The professional summarizing meetings Use Fireflies when your meetings are recurring calls on Zoom, Teams, or Meet and you want them captured without thinking about it. Use Notta when you record first and upload afterwards, or when a bot in the participant list would be awkward with clients. Either way, check your local consent rules and tell people they are being recorded. That is basic courtesy, and in some places it is also the law. The developer summarizing conference talks Start with Ask YouTube to settle whether a talk deserves 45 minutes, then paste the transcript for anything you need to retain. What you want from a dense talk is usually specific , which is where a custom instruction beats a fixed template. If the talk covers tooling you are evaluating, AI coding assistants is a faster read. One adjacent tool is worth naming, precisely because it does the opposite job. Summarizing compresses a video that already exists. Generating an explainer produces a video for a question that has no video yet. Scrimba Explain does the second: an MCP plugin that turns a question into a narrated video walkthrough, free during open beta. It is not a summarizer and does not belong in the table above, and like any AI tool it can make mistakes, so double-check anything important. If MCP is new to you, MCP tutorials and courses covers the protocol. Frequently Asked Questions What is the best free AI video summarizer? Gemini Notebook, if your video is a public YouTube URL with captions. Its free tier holds 50 sources per notebook and answers across all of them at once. For a single video you are watching, YouTube's own Ask feature is free and instant, but exports nothing. Can AI summarize a video without captions or subtitles? Yes, but only tools running their own speech recognition, and they meter it. NoteGPT caps uncaptioned YouTube videos at 120 minutes on Pro. Gemini Notebook transcribes audio and video files you upload, but will not process an uncaptioned YouTube link. Notta and Fireflies transcribe audio directly. Are AI video summaries accurate? Accurate enough for triage, not reliable enough for anything consequential without checking. Summaries inherit every caption error beneath them, and Google warns automatic captions can misrepresent speech given accents or background noise. FaithBench found the best automated hallucination detectors catch unfaithful summaries only about half the time. Can ChatGPT or Claude summarize a YouTube video directly? Not reliably from a link alone. The dependable method is opening YouTube's transcript panel, copying the text, and pasting it into the assistant with your own instructions. You lose timestamps and it stays manual, but you gain full control of the output format. Is it legal to summarize someone else's video? Summarizing a video for your own study or notes is generally uncontroversial. Republishing a full transcript, or a substantial summary presented as your own content, depends on your jurisdiction and the platform's terms. For recorded meetings, consent rules are the more pressing issue. Key Takeaways Most AI video summarizers never process video. They read the transcript, so captions decide which tools can help you. Google documents six reasons automatic captions fail to generate, among them poor audio, overlapping speakers, and unsupported languages. Gemini Notebook is the strongest free option for captioned YouTube videos, at 50 sources per notebook. NoteGPT is the only tool here that publicly prices uncaptioned video, capping it at 120 minutes on Pro. Meetings need a different product. Fireflies joins calls, Notta imports recordings, and both transcribe audio rather than captions. Pasting a transcript into an assistant you already pay for costs nothing and gives the most control. Sources Vendor pricing and feature claims are self-reported, checked August 2026. YouTube Help. "Use automatic captioning." https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6373554 YouTube Help. title: iHeartMedia’s My Cultura Podcast Network and Futuro Media Debut “Muy Excited with Maria Garcia,” A New Weekly Podcast Exploring the Moments That Shape Pop Culture
summary: iHeartMedia is a leading global media and entertainment company specializing in radio, digital, mobile, social, live events and on-demand entertainment.
body_text: Hosted by acclaimed writer and award-winning podcast creator Maria Garcia, the series unpacks the moments, music, movies and memories that continue to define generations WHAT: My Cultura, iHeartMedia’s podcast network dedicated to elevating Latino voices and stories, and Futuro Media today announced the debut of "Muy Excited with Maria Garcia," a new weekly audio and video podcast hosted by award-winning writer, editor and podcast creator Maria Garcia. Each week, Garcia will choose a nostalgic or contemporary piece of culture, whether it's an iconic album, unforgettable film, defining cultural moment or major event, and unpacks its lasting impact through humor, storytelling and insightful cultural analysis. "Muy Excited" will explore why the stories we share and the culture we consume continue to shape our identities, relationships and understanding of the world. In the premiere episode, Garcia will revisit Ricky Martin's extraordinary career and cultural legacy after a performance during Bad Bunny's "Benito Bowl" sparks an unexpected conversation with her 11-year-old son. Exploring how Martin's groundbreaking success paved the way for artists like Bad Bunny to embrace their identity and politics unapologetically, Garcia will examine what one unforgettable performance reveals about Latino culture across generations. Throughout the season, listeners will hear immersive storytelling, personal anecdotes from Maria and incisive analysis on music, movies, cultural phenomena and defining moments that continue to resonate across generations. WHO: Garcia is the Executive Editor of Futuro Studios, where she has created and overseen multiple award-winning podcasts. She is the creator and host of the critically acclaimed "Anything for Selena," which was named one of the year's best podcasts by The Atlantic, Vulture, TIME and Vogue, among many others. She was also named newcomer of the year by Apple Podcasts in 2021. Her Apple Original series "My Divo," exploring Mexican icon Juan Gabriel alongside her own queer and Mexican roots, debuted at No. 1 in its category in 2024. In 2025, Apple Podcasts recognized Garcia as one of its "Creators We Love." WHEN: The series premieres today, July 30, 2026, with new episodes available weekly. WHERE: “Muy Excited with Maria Garcia'' is distributed by iHeartPodcasts and is available on the iHeartRadio app and everywhere podcasts are heard, with full video episodes available on YouTube . About Futuro Media Futuro Media is an independent, nonprofit news organization and podcast studio founded in 2010 by Pulitzer Prize winner Maria Hinojosa. Based in Harlem, New York, Futuro Media produces the Peabody Award-winning Latino USA, the longest-running Latino news and cultural program in public radio, which celebrated 33 years on the air. Its podcast studio, Futuro Studios, is home to the Pulitzer Prize-winning Suave and acclaimed series La Brega and Anything for Selena. Futuro Investigates, its IRE and Murrow award-winning investigative journalism unit, produced After Uvalde: Guns, Grief & Texas Politics. About My Cultura Podcast Network iHeartMedia’s My Cultura Podcast Network launched May 2021 in collaboration with Enrique Santos, iHeartMedia’s top-rated on-air personality and President and Chief Creative Officer of iHeartLatino, and has since welcomed actor, producer, entrepreneur and activist Wilmer Valderrama along with Eva Longoria and her studio Hyphenate Media Group as stakeholders. Since launch, the network has seen steady listener growth and has become home to more than 60 podcasts including hit series “ Chiquis and Chill ,” “ The Moment with Jorge Ramos and Paola Ramos ,” “ Bleep! with Ana Navarro ,” “ Against All Odds with Yris Palmer ,” “ More Better with Stephanie & Melissa ,” “ Princess of South Beach, '' “ Sacred Scandal ,” “ Radio Ambulante ,” “ Magical Rewind, ” “ Agushto Papá ,” “ Enrique Santos Podcast ,” “ Suite 305 with Lele Pons ,” “ Dos Amigos with Wilmer Valderrama ,” “ Latino USA ,” and many more. All My Cultura shows are distributed by iHeartPodcasts. Listeners can find the full catalog of My Cultura podcasts here .

title: Lichtiger Score for Severe Ulcerative Colitis Explained
summary: Separate the Lichtiger symptom score from lab-based severe UC criteria.
body_text: The Lichtiger Index is an eight-part clinical score used in ulcerative colitis studies, especially severe or hospitalized disease . It records diarrhea, nighttime diarrhea, visible blood, fecal incontinence, abdominal pain or cramping, general well-being, abdominal tenderness, and antidiarrheal-drug use. The score itself contains no CRP, ESR, hemoglobin, albumin, or fecal calprotectin. It is sometimes called a modified Truelove and Witts index, which creates a naming trap: the classic Truelove and Witts criteria used to define acute severe UC include systemic and laboratory findings ( IBD activity-index review ; acute severe UC review ). What the Lichtiger score asks The index assigns points to daily stool frequency and adds separate weight for nocturnal diarrhea . Visible blood is graded by its proportion of stools. Incontinence, cramping, and antidiarrheal use add points, while well-being and abdominal tenderness are graded by severity. The total ranges from 0 to 21, with higher scores representing greater clinical activity. Trials have used thresholds and reductions in the score to define response or remission, but definitions should be read from the protocol. A hospital team may collect the components daily to follow a trajectory. The direction and speed of change can be more useful than attaching a generic label to one total. Several inputs can be influenced by problems other than mucosal inflammation. Infection, medication effects , reduced intake, and other gastrointestinal conditions can affect stool frequency and pain. Antidiarrheal use is particularly contextual because these medicines may be inappropriate in some severe-colitis situations. Do not take one to improve a score without the treating team’s guidance. Why this is not the same as the ASUC definition Classic Truelove and Witts severe colitis requires frequent bloody stools plus at least one sign of systemic toxicity, historically including fever, tachycardia, anemia, or raised ESR. Modern practice may use CRP in related assessments. That is a definition used to identify acute severe ulcerative colitis, a medical emergency requiring hospital care, not the same calculation as the symptom-focused Lichtiger total ( UC severity review ; acute severe UC review ). Hospital teams also use day-three prediction tools to estimate risk of intravenous-steroid failure. The Oxford criteria combine stool frequency and CRP; other tools can incorporate albumin or colonic dilation. Those scores answer a treatment-response question and should not be mislabeled as Lichtiger. Where labs and endoscopy fit Although labs are absent from Lichtiger, CBC, CRP, electrolytes , renal function, and albumin can be crucial in severe colitis. Stool testing can look for infection. Imaging may assess dilation or complications, and limited endoscopic evaluation can help confirm severity and collect biopsies. Guidelines and reviews emphasize this multi-part inpatient assessment rather than relying on one symptom index ( acute severe UC review ). If a Lichtiger score appears in a record, save the date, individual answers, and whether the patient was hospitalized. Add vital signs, stool-test results, hemoglobin, CRP, albumin, electrolytes, imaging, and treatment timing. Rapidly worsening bloody diarrhea, fever, fast heart rate, fainting, severe pain or swelling, or dehydration warrants urgent evaluation. The score can structure clinical change, but it does not replace the laboratory and bedside assessment that makes severe UC safe to manage. Questions that make the number more useful Before comparing this result with an older one, confirm that both records used the same named instrument, version, scoring range, and assessment window. Ask whether the total represents the worst segment, a sum across segments, an average, or a single day. If a clinician or study used a modified version, record exactly what was removed or added. Also check whether treatment, bowel preparation, infection, missed diary entries, or incomplete examination affected the inputs. A small apparent change may reflect measurement conditions rather than a meaningful change in disease. At a visit, useful questions include: What domain does this score measure? Which component drove the result? What would count as response or remission in this setting? Does the number need confirmation with blood work, stool testing, endoscopy, biopsy, or imaging? Is the goal to follow symptoms, current inflammation, structural damage, treatment response, or quality of life? Asking these questions turns an unfamiliar total into a specific clinical conversation. For personal tracking , avoid combining unlike scores on one graph. Keep each instrument in its own series and place objective tests on parallel timelines. Save the source report because the component details may matter later. Note both the sample or procedure date and the date you received the result. Trends are easiest to interpret when the method and timing stay consistent. If the number conflicts with how you feel or with another test, bring the disagreement to your care team instead of choosing the result that seems most reassuring. Discordance is often the reason to look more closely. This article is for educational purposes and is not medical advice. It is researched against current AGA clinical guidelines and peer-reviewed sources. Always discuss treatment decisions with your care team. title: Caldwell ClayCopter Surface-to-Air™ Wins 2026 Frank Desomma Innovation of the Year Award
summary: (Columbia, MO) August __, 2026 – Caldwell®, a leading innovator in shooting and range equipment, today announced that its ClayCopter Surface-to-Air™ Pro Kit has won the 2026 Frank Desomma Innovation of the Year Award from the Industry Choice Awards (ICA), marking the second consecutive year that Caldwell® has earned the prestigious honor. The annual award recognizes a single product that demonstrates exceptional innovation, design, or performance that stands out in the outdoor industry – this year, ICA chose to recognize the latest evolution of Caldwell’s ClayCopter® platform and its most advanced launcher to date, the ClayCopter Surface-to-Air™ Launcher.Read Full Story >>
body_text: Tags Source: Caldwell® PDF Version (Columbia, MO) August __, 2026 – Caldwell®, a leading innovator in shooting and range equipment, today announced that its ClayCopter Surface-to-Air™ Pro Kit has won the 2026 Frank Desomma Innovation of the Year Award from the Industry Choice Awards (ICA), marking the second consecutive year that Caldwell® has earned the prestigious honor. The annual award recognizes a single product that demonstrates exceptional innovation, design, or performance that stands out in the outdoor industry – this year, ICA chose to recognize the latest evolution of Caldwell’s ClayCopter® platform and its most advanced launcher to date, the ClayCopter Surface-to-Air™ Launcher. Introduced in 2025, the original ClayCopter® gave target shooters an exciting new alternative to traditional clay targets with a lightweight, handheld motorized launcher capable of sending biodegradable ClayCopter® targets out to 100 yards. Caldwell® has since expanded ClayCopter® into a connected ecosystem that establishes an entirely new target throwing platform for recreational shooters, competitors and commercial range operators. At the center of that expansion is the ClayCopter Surface-to-Air™ Launcher, a portable, ground-based system that provides hands-free operation and varied target presentations, including incoming, crossing, wobbling and oscillating throws. Integrated with the Caldwell Clays™ App, the ClayCopter Surface-to-Air™ enables full control over multiple wireless launchers using Caldwell’s proprietary Touch-to-Launch technology – creating a dynamic, customizable sporting clays experience virtually anywhere. “We are incredibly honored to have the ClayCopter Surface-to-Air™ recognized with the Frank Desomma Innovation of the Year Award,” said James Tayon, Chief Product Officer. “This recognition means a great deal to our team because the award is an unbiased evaluation of all products in the shooting sports industry – and Caldwell® came out on top. The Surface-to-Air represents what we believe innovation should be – solving consumer problems, challenging the conventions of established categories, and creating entirely new experiences rather than simply incrementally improving what already exists. Our goal is to develop products that make shooting sports more engaging and accessible, create new reasons to participate, and ultimately bring new consumers into the sport. I’m extremely proud of the team that turned that vision into the ClayCopter Surface-to-Air™, and grateful to the Industry Choice Awards for recognizing what they created.” The Industry Choice Awards, sponsored and administered by Oneida Molded Plastics, use a structured evaluation process with 20–30 experienced firearms-industry evaluators unaffiliated with participating companies. Products are assessed in retail- and range-type environments across fit, form and function, with Oneida having no influence over evaluation data or rankings. The Innovation of the Year Award honors Frank Desomma, a three-time ICA Rifle of the Year winner and 2018 American Rifleman Golden Bullseye Award recipient. About Caldwell® Caldwell® is a leading shooting accessory brand within the American Outdoor Brands, Inc. portfolio. Trusted by firearms owners for over two decades, Caldwell® innovates new products to Eliminate the Variables That Make You Miss™. The Caldwell® name represents the brand’s ongoing commitment to bringing innovative and problem-solving products to the target shooting category. For more information on Caldwell® products, including the Caldwell Clays™ App and the entire family of smart launchers, visit https://www.caldwellshooting.com/claycopter . title: Best Time of the Year to Build a Pool
summary: When is the best time to build a pool? Find out how costs, climate, and scheduling impact your project—and why fall and winter can save you more.
body_text: Building a breathtaking new backyard pool takes a little planning ahead. From thinking about how a pool will complement your lifestyle to the logistics of when to build, doing your homework beforehand can make pool ownership all the more rewarding. Thanks to modern construction technology, swimming pools can be built and installed at any time of year. That said, there are factors that make certain seasons better for building than others. Where you live, geographic characteristics, weather considerations, and more can play a role in determining when is the best time to break ground on a new pool. For instance, in northern parts of the country, winter weather can freeze the ground and slow down pool construction, resulting in a longer and more expensive building process. By determining the best time of year to build a pool in your region, you can save money while ensuring your new pool is ready on time. Keep reading to learn about the best time to build a pool based on your location, budget, and when you want your personal pool season to kick off. What Affects the Best Time to Build a Pool? There are multiple factors that influence what time of year is best for building a pool. Some examples include your region’s climate and weather, your target date for opening the pool, seasonal contractor availability and pricing, and your pool construction budget. From an aesthetic standpoint, giving your lawn time to recover from excavation and construction is also an important factor for many homeowners. Every season has its own unique pros and cons for building. We’ll compare each of them later in this guide. But first, let’s take a closer look at how the time of year impacts building costs, construction timelines, and post-construction yard recovery. Budget and Costs Pool installation costs fluctuate with consumer demand, which peaks in spring and summer before dropping again in fall and winter. That means it’s usually cheaper to build a pool between September and February, and costlier between March and August. Suppliers typically raise prices during springtime, with costs falling again during autumn and winter, when builders offer seasonal discounts. No matter what time of year you start building, there are a variety of loans and financing options to help you manage the costs of building a beautiful new pool. Learn more about pool financing , or use Latham’s pool cost estimator to start calculating your budget. Weather and Climate It’s important to consider how weather might affect your project. Conditions like heavy rain, extreme heat, or frozen ground can all cause delays. On the flipside, mild weather and a lack of precipitation can pave a faster, smoother path to construction. Depending on which part of the United States you live in, it may be a good strategy to avoid building in winter and aim for late summer or early fall, when conditions tend to be driest with the lowest risk of a ground freeze. While weather can impact timelines and costs, it won’t affect the quality of your completed inground pool. As long as you work with a trusted and experienced builder, you can expect a stunning finished result all year-round. Landscaping and Yard Recovery To install an inground pool, it’s necessary to dig out and excavate parts of your yard. That means your lawn and garden will temporarily be disrupted. Building your pool during fall or winter gives your lawn the maximum amount of time to recover and start regrowing before summer weather returns in full swing. If the appearance of your landscaping is a top priority for you, off-season construction might be the most satisfying approach to installing a pool. Pros and Cons by Season Every season has its own advantages and drawbacks to building a pool. Here are a few at-a-glance points to consider when determining what time of year to start your project: Winter — Winter is typically the cheapest time of year to build a pool, plus the easiest time of year to schedule a contractor due to lack of seasonal demand. However, if you live in a cold climate, ice, snow, or freezing temperatures could interfere with construction. Spring — Spring typically brings favorable weather for construction, but contractors tend to be busy and charge higher prices at this time of year, since spring is also the lead-up to peak pool season. Summer — Prices peak in summer and contractors are already heavily booked, but the long days and clear weather support fast construction. Fall — Fall is an affordable time of year to build, and also gives your landscaping time to recover. However, your project could be delayed by early frosts and cold, hard ground depending on your location. Building a Pool in Fall Fall is an ideal time of year to build a pool, especially toward the middle or beginning of the season before the risk of an early freeze becomes too great. Demand for pool construction dips during autumn, which means contractors charge lower rates and have more scheduling flexibility, creating a win-win situation for homeowners. As an added bonus, fall construction gives your landscaping ample time to recover before summer swim season. Building a Pool in Spring While not without some potential drawbacks, spring is generally considered a good time of year to install a pool. Building during spring allows enough time to get your new pool ready by summer, especially since mild spring weather typically favors speedy construction. The disadvantage is that contractors’ schedules tend to fill up quickly as clients rush to book builders ahead of summer. This high demand also makes spring an expensive time to build. Another location-dependent drawback is that some regions, like Texas , receive heavy spring rains that can slow down construction. Building a Pool in Summer Like other seasons, summer has pros and cons when it comes to building a pool. Depending where you live, summer often brings dry weather patterns that create just the right conditions for faster, more efficient construction. On the other hand, extreme summer heat can have the opposite effect, slowing down construction by making labor impossible. Another drawback is that summer is peak building season, which means pool contractors often have longer wait times, less flexible schedules, and higher prices at this time of year. Breaking ground on your pool in the summer also means that you have less time to enjoy your pool for the full duration of swim season. Starting before summer means that your pool will be swim-ready the moment the hottest days of the year set in. Building a Pool in Winter In states with warm climates, like Georgia and Arizona , winter is often the fastest and cheapest time of year to build a pool. However, that doesn’t apply to other regions of the U.S. In states that have cold winters, like New York or Illinois . In colder parts of the Midwest and Northeast, low temperatures can freeze the ground and lead to costly delays, defeating the purpose of building in winter in order to save money. Why Fall and Spring Are the Best (and Cheapest) Times to Build a Pool Depending on your location, spring and fall are typically the best seasons for pool construction. The advantage of building in spring is that it typically brings mild weather and dry ground, which allows construction to proceed with minimal hiccups. Additionally, you’ll avoid the summer rush by starting in spring. Building in fall also has major benefits. Like winter, fall is the cheapest time of year to build a pool. But unlike winter, fall doesn’t put you at high risk of freeze-related delays. Plus, your lawn will have extra time to recover and reach its full bloom before warm weather returns. There’s also another advantage to building during fall or spring: along with saving money and speeding up construction, it also ensures that your pool will be ready to use and enjoy by summer. Save Money on Materials and Labor Consumer demand for pool construction peaks in summer and spring, then declines again during the fall-winter off-season. To attract more business during this slower period, many builders offer discounted rates in fall and winter, which means you can potentially get the same services for less money. In particular, building before the new year can help you lock in lower costs ahead of supplier price increases. Faster Construction Timelines Pool contractors have fewer clients to juggle during the off-season. That means construction crews have more time and resources to focus on your project, resulting in greater efficiency and faster pool building timelines . During this time of year, there are also shorter wait times for city inspections and permits, which means you can check off legal requirements quickly. Weather-related delays can potentially slow down construction progress, but are less likely to occur during spring and fall compared to other times of year, like winter (which can bring freezes) or summer (which can bring extreme heat). Flexible Scheduling Even in climates that stay warm year-round, summertime is still the peak season for swimming. That means demand is greater, contractors are busier, and — arguably the biggest drawback — prices are higher. If you start construction during the fall or winter off-season when builders have better availability, you’ll have more freedom and flexibility to schedule construction at a time that’s convenient for your family. Ready-to-Swim by Summer One of the key advantages to building in the off-season is that it ensures your new pool will be ready to open when warm summer weather arrives. That means you can start enjoying your new pool immediately, instead of waiting around for summer construction to wrap up. Not only does getting an early headstart enable your pool to open for summer, the off-season also tends to be the cheapest time of year to build. Plus, an off-season start gives you plenty of time to handle permits and inspections while avoiding the summer rush. How Climate and Location Affect the Best Time to Build a Pool In southern states with hot climates, such as Florida and Texas, there’s little risk of encountering snowstorms or freezing winter weather. Winter is also outside of the pocket of storm-season that typically hits the Southern and Southwestern portions of the U.S., too. Fall and winter are normally the most affordable times of year to build, which is due to a combination of decreased consumer demand and seasonal contractor discounts. In central and northern regions of the United States, like New England or the Pacific Northwest, frigid winter temperatures can slow or halt construction as soil freezes, ice accumulates, and snow packs into excavation areas. To avoid these potential roadblocks, it’s typically more practical — and less expensive — to build during spring or autumn instead of winter. From a weather perspective, summer can also be a good time for construction in cold climates — but on the other hand, is an expensive and busy season. No matter where you live, it’s a good idea to research how your local climate and geography might impact pool construction. You may want to look into issues like sandy vs. clay-heavy soil, seasonal heavy rains or flooding, and how high the water table is in your area. Planning Ahead for Your Pool Project Even off-season construction projects require months of planning. To make sure your project is completed on schedule, it’s critical to get an early start. By starting to plan your pool at least 6 months before your target pool opening date, you’ll give yourself plenty of time to contact a builder, put together a budget, finalize your pool design, and obtain the proper permits to break ground on your new pool. Starting early also creates a time cushion in the event that your project runs into weather-related delays, such as flooding, freezing, or wildfires. Depending on factors like how large the excavation site is, what materials you choose, and how long it takes to obtain the required permits and inspections, the pool installation process can take anywhere from several weeks to over 6 months. So, When Is the Best Time to Build a Pool? From a financial standpoint, fall and winter are typically the cheapest times of year to build a pool. However, the best time of year to build a pool depends not only on your budget, but also the climate and weather where you live. In most parts of the United States, spring and early-to-mid-autumn are considered ideal pool building seasons due to contractor availability and low risk of extreme weather. Ultimately, no matter when you build, the best strategy is to start planning early and book your contractor months in advance. Taking a proactive approach will help ensure that your new swimming pool is ready to enjoy by summer. It’s equally important to choose a properly licensed, highly rated pool builder. At Latham, we have over 70 years of experience designing and installing custom pools throughout the United States, making us one of the nation’s most trusted and well-established industry leaders. Contact us today to connect with a local Latham builder near you. Frequently Asked Questions About Building a Pool Researching the pool construction process is the best way to ensure that your project proceeds smoothly. Below, you’ll find quick answers to some of the most frequently asked questions about building residential pools, including when to book a contractor, what financing options are available, and whether there are drawbacks to building in the off-season. When you work with a licensed, experienced pool builder like the independent professionals at Latham, you can expect top quality craftsmanship — no matter what time of year construction begins. That said, there are some unique challenges to building a pool in the off-season, which could impact the timeline and cost of your project. For example, in some regions freezing winter temperatures could slow down or postpone construction, while also preventing pool materials like concrete from setting properly. It’s generally recommended to book a pool contractor at least 3 to 6 months in advance. However, booking a contractor is only one step of the pool planning process, which you should ideally begin at least 6 to 12 months in advance. This allows adequate time for other critical steps, such as finalizing the pool design, excavating your property, installing electrical systems, and securing the necessary building permits, which can vary in terms of timing, depending on your location. Yes! No matter what time of year you decide to start building a pool, you can explore a variety of loans and financing methods to make owning a pool a reality. Depending on your credit history and other financial factors, types of pool financing options that you can qualify for year-round include personal loans, home equity loans, and home equity lines of credit (HELOCs). Summertime is peak pool season, but also has some drawbacks and hidden costs that can make it a less than ideal time to begin construction. Due to high demand during summer, pool contractors typically charge more and have less availability compared to other times of year. Regardless of the climate or season, hidden costs can also arise before, during, or after construction, such as dirt or debris removal, retaining wall construction, and the installation of child safety fencing, which is required by state law in most U.S. locations. title: Federal Contract Insurance Checklist (2026)
summary: Insurance requirements for US government contractors: required coverages, typical limits, FAR minimums, required endorsements, Defense Base Act (DBA) coverage for overseas work, AM Best guidance, and the procurement mistakes that delay contract starts.
body_text: What insurance is required for a US government contract? FAR Subpart 28.3 sets the baseline: Workers' Compensation and Employer's Liability, Commercial General Liability, and Automobile Liability, plus Aircraft or Vessel liability where the work involves them. The FAR minimums are floors, not targets. Your solicitation, contracting officer, or prime usually requires higher limits, and DoD contracts add cyber and safeguarding obligations through DFARS 252.204-7012 and CMMC. Always read the insurance clause in your own solicitation. What are the FAR minimum insurance limits? Under FAR 28.307-2, the stated minimums are: Employer's Liability at least $100,000; Comprehensive General Liability at least $500,000 per occurrence for bodily injury; and Automobile Liability at $200,000 per person and $500,000 per occurrence for bodily injury, with $20,000 per occurrence for property damage. Aircraft liability is $200,000 per person and $500,000 per occurrence for bodily injury (other than passengers), $200,000 per occurrence for property damage, and passenger bodily injury of at least $200,000 multiplied by the number of seats. These are minimums only; most real contracts require $1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate or more. Do small businesses and startups need insurance to win federal contracts? Yes. Whether you bid directly or subcontract to a prime, the insurance clause flows down to you. Most solicitations will not let you begin performance, and many will not let you receive award, until you show a certificate of insurance meeting the contract's requirements. Buying coverage after you win, during the September fiscal year-end rush, is the single most common cause of delayed contract starts. What AM Best rating do federal contracts require? The FAR itself does not name a rating, but agencies and primes commonly require carriers rated A- VII or A- VIII or better by AM Best. A rated carrier is strongly recommended regardless, because a certificate is worthless if the insurer behind it cannot pay a claim. You can check any carrier's rating free at ratings.ambest.com. What endorsements do federal and prime contracts require? The common trio is Additional Insured (naming the government or prime as insured on your policy), Primary and Non-Contributory (your policy pays first), and Waiver of Subrogation (your insurer gives up its right to pursue the other party). A certificate that shows the right limits but omits these endorsements is routinely rejected at compliance review. What is DBA insurance, and is it required for government contracts? DBA insurance is Defense Base Act coverage: a workers'-compensation-type policy required whenever your employees work outside the United States on a US government contract. When it applies it is mandatory under the Defense Base Act, and an ordinary state Workers' Compensation policy will not respond to an overseas claim. It is placed as a separate specialty policy, FAR 52.228-3 is the clause that flows it down, and a contracting officer will not authorize overseas performance without it. What other insurance do overseas government contractors need? Beyond Defense Base Act coverage, contractors with staff working abroad commonly add a cluster of overseas lines: foreign voluntary workers' compensation (to fill gaps the DBA does not reach and coordinate home-country benefits), war risk and terrorism cover (for higher-risk regions), kidnap and ransom with emergency evacuation, and international medical and travel coverage. Which of these apply depends on where your people are deployed, so flag any overseas scope to your broker before award. These are specialty placements with longer lead times than domestic coverage. What insurance does a defense startup need for a government contract? The FAR core stack (Workers' Comp and Employer's Liability, General Liability, Auto), plus the coverages your scope triggers such as Tech E&O and Cyber. What sets defense apart is the compliance stack that rides alongside the insurance clause: DFARS 252.204-7012 and CMMC for safeguarding data, ITAR and EAR for export control, Section 889 for prohibited equipment, and the Defense Base Act if any employee works overseas. The insurance and the compliance flow-downs are checked together, so plan for both before award. What insurance does a space company need for a government contract? Beyond the FAR core stack, space contractors face exposures standard commercial liability excludes: aviation or UAS liability (a drone is legally an aircraft), pre-launch and launch liability, in-orbit or satellite coverage, and third-party launch liability required by a federal launch license. These are specialty placements with a small set of carriers and longer lead times, so a space startup should start the insurance conversation well before a September award. How much does government contractor insurance cost? It depends on the coverages and limits your contract requires, plus your revenue, headcount, and claims history. As a planning range for an early-stage startup buying each line on its own: General Liability often runs $500 to $2,000 a year, Tech E&O $1,500 to $5,000, and Cyber $1,500 to $8,000 or more, with Workers' Comp priced off payroll. Higher required limits and specialty lines (aviation, launch, Defense Base Act) raise the total, while the required endorsements usually add little or nothing. The fastest way to a firm number is to send your contract's insurance exhibit to a broker for live quotes.

title: ZIONS BANCORPORATION COMPLETES ACQUISITION OF FANNIE MAE AND FREDDIE MAC MULTIFAMILY BUSINESS LINE FROM BASIS INVESTMENT GROUP
summary: /PRNewswire/ -- Zions Bancorporation, National Association (NASDAQ: ZION) today announced it has completed its previously announced acquisition of the agency...
body_text: SALT LAKE CITY , Aug. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Zions Bancorporation, National Association (NASDAQ: ZION ) today announced it has completed its previously announced acquisition of the agency lending platform of Basis Multifamily Finance I, LLC, a subsidiary of Basis Investment Group, LLC, (collectively, "Basis"), a national commercial real estate debt and equity investment platform. The acquisition includes the agency lending platform's experienced team, capabilities, and all associated mortgage servicing rights. The acquisition expands Zions' product suite through participation in the Fannie Mae DUS® program and Freddie Mac's Optigo® Conventional program, expanding the bank's ability to meet the financing needs of multifamily owners, operators, and developers nationwide. "This acquisition bolsters our ability to serve our customers across the multifamily housing sector and is a natural extension of our commitment to supporting the development and preservation of the full spectrum of multifamily products, including workforce and affordable housing," said Harris Simmons, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Zions Bancorporation. "We look forward to working closely with Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac and are pleased to welcome Basis' agency lending team to Zions as we continue to grow our multifamily business and meet the evolving needs of our customers." "I am excited to see the Basis Multifamily team begin their next chapter with Zions. Our strategic partnership with Zions brings together the strengths of both organizations, expanding investment and financing opportunities in affordable and workforce housing across our fund platforms while creating long-term value for our clients, investors, and communities. I wish Zions and the agency team every success as they scale the platform and take it to the next level," said Tammy K. Jones, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Basis. Advisors Zions Capital Markets served as financial advisor to Zions, with Allen Overy Shearman Sterling US LLP as legal advisor. Beekman Advisors served as financial advisor to Basis, with Davis Polk & Wardwell LLP as legal advisor. About Zions Bancorporation Zions Bancorporation, N.A. is one of the nation's premier financial services companies with approximately $89 billion of total assets at December 31, 2025, and annual net revenue of $3.4 billion in 2025. Zions operates under local management teams and distinct brands in 11 western states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Texas, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming. The Bank is a consistent recipient of national and state-wide customer survey awards in small- and middle-market banking, as well as a leader in public finance advisory services and Small Business Administration lending. In addition, Zions is included in the S&P MidCap 400 and NASDAQ Financial 100 indices. Investor information and links to local banking brands can be accessed at www.zionsbancorporation.com . Zions Capital Markets conducts the capital markets and investment banking activities of Zions Bancorporation. For more information and important disclosures please visit www.zionscapitalmarkets.com . About Basis Investment Group Basis Investment Group is a diversified commercial real estate investment management platform with more than $9.2 billion in debt and equity transactions closed across 47 states. Basis is a Registered Investment Advisor (RIA), direct lender, and investor, providing financing and investment solutions across all middle-market commercial real estate sectors, including affordable and workforce housing, throughout the United States. For more information, please visit www.basisinvgroup.com . title: Legal Knowledge Management Software: 7 Options by Context
summary: Compare seven legal knowledge management tools by the context they manage, from precedents and expertise to live matters, with a practical pilot checklist.
body_text: Back to insights Legal Knowledge Management Software: 7 Options by Context August 14, 2026 &AI Team Legal knowledge management software is often sold as one answer to scattered files, buried precedents, and vanished know-how. The category actually spans several layers: document systems, curated search, experience databases, intranets, and tools that keep the context of a live matter together. Choosing well starts with the question your team must answer and the context required to act on it. The right framework maps that job to a specific software layer instead of asking one platform to cover the whole stack. Key takeaways Legal knowledge management is broader than document search. A usable result includes the source, its relationships, its status, the user's access rights, and the purpose for which it was retained. Different questions require different context. Reusing an approved brief, finding an internal expert, following an intake process, and analyzing evidence in a live matter are separate jobs. We built &AI as an AI workspace for patent litigation. We help teams keep matter documents, research, analysis, charts, and drafts in working context. We do not replace a firmwide knowledge management system. Permissions, provenance, and lifecycle controls are buying requirements. An answer should inherit source access, identify its support, and distinguish current knowledge from superseded material. Pilot the complete workflow. Test retrieval, analysis, attorney review, and the final deliverable with realistic edge cases. A useful legal knowledge record carries context Legal knowledge management software captures, curates, organizes, retrieves, and reuses an organization's institutional knowledge. That knowledge may be a brief, research memo, clause, checklist, expert profile, matter history, or an attorney's reasoning about why a source mattered. A document becomes reusable knowledge when the system preserves five kinds of context: Context What it should answer Example Source What exact material supports the result? Document version, page, paragraph, figure, email, or timestamp Relationships What is the material connected to? Client, matter, party, jurisdiction, legal issue, claim, product, or author Status Can the team rely on it now? Draft, approved, current, superseded, withdrawn, or outcome-tested Access Who is authorized to retrieve and reuse it? Matter permissions, ethical walls, role, office, or client restriction Purpose Why was it kept, and what work should it support? Precedent, pitch, advice, investigation, invalidity position, or training Full-text search can find matching words while missing the reason a document was useful. An old motion may discuss the right issue and still be a poor precedent because it came from another jurisdiction, reflects a rejected argument, or has been superseded. Context turns retrieval into a legal decision the user can review. Match the software layer to the legal job The same source may pass through several systems. A document management system (DMS) can remain the controlled record, a KM platform can publish an approved version for cross-matter reuse, and a practice workspace can apply it to a current matter. Legal job Context the user needs Primary software layer Reuse a motion, memo, or deal precedent Issue, court, jurisdiction, outcome, approval status, and current version Curated KM search over a DMS Negotiate a contract Agreement type, clause history, approved fallback, risk position, and prior approvals Clause library, DMS, and contract workflow Analyze a dispute or investigation Parties, custodians, chronology, allegations, evidence, and workstream Matter workspace, e-discovery, and DMS Build a patent invalidity or infringement position Patent family, prosecution history, claim construction, prior art, product evidence, and limitation-level citations Patent-litigation workspace plus DMS or KM Find an internal expert or representative matter Lawyer role, industry, matter type, result, credentials, and relationship Experience management Follow a policy or standard operating procedure Owner, audience, effective date, steps, exceptions, and review date Intranet, wiki, or knowledge base This distinction matters when a buyer asks whether a platform “manages context.” Firmwide KM supports durable reuse across people and matters. A matter or practice workspace supports active analysis within a bounded job. Both can be valuable, and they carry different governance responsibilities. Where we fit: patent-litigation matter context We built our AI workspace for patent litigation around the context required to move from a patent dispute to reviewable work product. Within a matter, a team can work with patents, patent families, prosecution history, prior cases, prior art, product materials, analysis, charts, and drafts. The workflow connects three activities: Search and collect. Teams search patents, non-patent literature, and product evidence, then add relevant sources to the matter. Analyze in shared context. Attorneys can ask questions of documents, structure findings in tables, and assess invalidity or infringement positions against claim limitations. Build work product. Selected evidence flows into invalidity and evidence-of-use claim charts or grounded drafts. Pinpoint citations link the analysis back to passages, figures, and timestamps for attorney review. That is matter-context management for a defined patent-litigation workflow. We do not provide a firmwide precedent library, expertise directory, policy intranet, records program, prosecution docket, or general legal research database. Firms use us alongside those systems when the immediate job is patent-litigation analysis and work product. Seven legal knowledge management options by context These products solve different parts of the KM problem. The useful comparison is their primary context layer and the systems on which they depend. Software Primary context layer Best fit Main dependency or boundary iManage Insight+ Curated knowledge and matter discovery Teams centered on iManage Cloud Relies on iManage content and connected business metadata OpenText Legal Knowledge Management Federated enterprise search Large organizations with several repositories Requires connector, identity, metadata, and relevance work Lexsoft T3 Governed curation for iManage content KM teams and professional support lawyers Oriented around iManage Work NetDocuments Document record, search, and document analysis Teams consolidating matter documents in a legal DMS The organization still defines approved knowledge Litera Foundation Experience and credentials Firms finding experts, matters, and pitch evidence Depends on clean matter, finance, CRM, and people data Thomson Reuters West km Internal work product with legal research Westlaw-centered research workflows Scope depends on indexed sources and Westlaw access Microsoft SharePoint Operational guidance and intranet knowledge Microsoft 365 teams with contained use cases Legal governance and information architecture require design iManage Insight+: curated knowledge in iManage Cloud Insight+ connects documents, matters, curated collections, extended metadata, and business data within iManage Cloud. Its curation tools support submission, enrichment, publication, maintenance, and archiving. Ask Knowledge can return grounded answers from firm-approved material while inheriting iManage security and ethical walls. It fits organizations that already use iManage Work and want a native route from matter content to governed knowledge. OpenText Legal Knowledge Management: federated search OpenText searches structured and unstructured sources such as DMS libraries, matter and billing data, attorney profiles, email, file shares, intranets, portals, and dockets. It adds classification, concept search, predictive search, visualization, and text mining while respecting permissions from connected systems. This model fits an organization whose knowledge remains distributed. Connector coverage, identity mapping, metadata quality, and relevance tuning determine the result. Lexsoft T3: governed curation over iManage Work Lexsoft T3 adds knowledge submission, extraction, classification, taxonomy control, publication workflows, search, analytics, and redaction around content in iManage Work. It suits knowledge managers and professional support lawyers who need a formal path from matter material to approved know-how. The selection should account for approval paths, ethical walls, redaction rules, jurisdictions, and languages. NetDocuments: a DMS and document-knowledge foundation NetDocuments combines cloud document and email management with version control, optical character recognition, profiling, search, collaboration, automation, and AI analysis over authorized files. It is a fit when the first problem is scattered matter content or a weak system of record. The platform can surface knowledge from documents, while the firm still owns precedent approval, review dates, retention, and withdrawal rules. Litera Foundation: experience and credentials context Foundation connects client, matter, lawyer, and party data so firms can find representative matters, relevant experience, internal experts, relationships, and pricing context. That supports pitches, staffing, cross-selling, and practice analysis. Its center of gravity is structured experience. A separate repository and curation process remain necessary for the briefs, templates, and precedents behind that experience. Thomson Reuters West km: work product in research context West km indexes an organization's work product and combines retrieval with Westlaw, WestSearch, and KeyCite. It fits teams that want prior internal analysis beside external legal research. Buyers should map the repositories to be indexed, document-version behavior, permissions, and required Westlaw access. Experience data, policy guidance, and practice-specific work-product assembly sit in other layers. Microsoft SharePoint: configurable operational knowledge SharePoint provides sites, pages, libraries, lists, metadata, versioning, search, permissions, and Microsoft 365 integration. SharePoint agents can answer questions from selected sites, pages, folders, and files according to each user's existing access. It works for policies, checklists, practice pages, training, and curated guidance. Legal taxonomies, ethical walls, review ownership, retention, and search tuning require deliberate administration. How to evaluate legal knowledge management software Start with one sentence: “An authorized user needs to find or produce ___ from ___ in order to ___.” This exposes the source systems, access model, context, and required output before a demonstration begins. Evaluation question Evidence to require in a pilot Does it complete the job? Time from question through source review, correction, approval, and usable output Does access remain correct? Results before and after an ethical wall, role change, document move, and matter closure Does it preserve context? Source version, pinpoint support, matter relationships, status, date, and approval owner Can the team govern the lifecycle? Steps to submit, redact, approve, publish, update, supersede, withdraw, retain, and delete material Can attorneys review AI output? Citations for material statements, visible source passages, correction controls, and an audit trail Can the organization operate it? Implementation, connectors, migration, taxonomy work, training, support, and ongoing owner time Efficiency should be measured across the whole workflow. The 2024 ABA AI TechReport found that 54.4% of respondents selected saving time or increasing efficiency as AI's most important potential benefit. A fast answer creates little value when an attorney must reconstruct its sources or formatting. AI review also belongs inside the confidentiality and professional-responsibility review. ABA Formal Opinion 512 applies existing duties of competence, confidentiality, communication, candor, supervision, and reasonable fees to generative AI. The vendor assessment should cover retention, model training, subprocessors, human access, encryption, audit logs, data location, deletion, and incident response. Our guide to confidential patent work provides a detailed checklist for patent teams. Use realistic failure cases in the pilot: a known useful precedent, a superseded version, a scanned PDF, a misfiled document, a restricted matter, and a question whose answer spans two sources. The result should be a workflow decision based on permission, provenance, and output quality, rather than a feature score. Frequently asked questions What is the difference between a DMS and legal knowledge management software? A DMS stores, versions, secures, and retrieves documents and email. Legal KM adds curation, context, approval, expertise, and cross-matter reuse. Some platforms span both categories through connected modules, but the operating decisions remain distinct. Is a matter workspace the same as a legal KM system? No. A matter workspace keeps the sources, people, analysis, decisions, and deliverables for active work together. A legal KM system preserves approved knowledge for authorized reuse across matters and over time. A team may use both, with the DMS serving as the controlled record. Can SharePoint serve as a law firm's knowledge management system? Yes, for contained use cases such as policies, checklists, training, practice pages, and curated libraries. The firm must design metadata, permissions, ethical-wall handling, review ownership, search, retention, and content lifecycle rules. Does AI remove the need to tag and curate legal knowledge? No. AI can extract metadata, classify documents, suggest relationships, and answer questions over authorized material. Human owners still decide what is authoritative, who may use it, when it needs review, and when it should be withdrawn. How much does legal knowledge management software cost? Specialist legal KM products generally use custom quotes. Total cost depends on users, repositories, connectors, migration, data volume, AI usage, security requirements, and implementation. Include content cleanup, taxonomy work, training, administration, and ongoing legal review in the comparison. If your immediate gap is patent-litigation matter context, start your 7-day free trial and take one current matter from source search through citation review and export.
